testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: How much steering wheel play is acceptable?
questions.explanation: Steering wheel play should not exceed 10 degrees. Too much play makes steering difficult and unsafe.

questions.question: What should you do when construction workers are near the road?

options.text: Wait to proceed until the construction is complete.

questions.explanation: Slow down when construction workers are near the roadway. Follow the posted speed limits in construction zones.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Steer with one hand to keep the other hand free.

questions.explanation: Slow down in work zones. Follow posted speed limits and drive even slower if workers are nearby or if road conditions are poor.

questions.question: What can extremely hot temperatures cause?
questions.explanation: Heat causes air to expand, which increases tire pressure. High pressure can cause tire failure. Check tire pressure regularly in hot weather.

questions.question: What does the suspension system do?

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load the proper distance behind the driver's compartment.
Maintains a safe distance between the vehicle and other vehicles.
Lightens the load for the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. Suspension damage is very dangerous.

questions.question: At what air pressure level will an air compressor governor stop pumping air?
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping when air tanks reach 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: What should you do before driving downhill?

options.text: Take your vehicle out of gear.
Rely only on braking to reduce your speed.

questions.explanation: Shift into a lower gear before going downhill. Use the engine to slow the vehicle. Relying only on brakes can cause them to overheat and fail.

questions.question: When checking springs during a vehicle inspection, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Ensure torsion springs are not damaged.

questions.explanation: Check for missing, broken, or cracked springs. Do not glue or repair damaged springs. Damaged suspension parts must be replaced, not repaired.

questions.question: How is friction created inside a brake drum?

options.text: Push against the inside of the drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push against the inside of the drum.
questions.explanation: Brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum to create friction. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: What condition should the exhaust system be in?
questions.explanation: The exhaust system must be fastened securely with no loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: During exercises other than straight line backing, how many times may you exit your vehicle to check its position?
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during skills tests. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you may look one time. For other exercises, you may look two times.

questions.question: When should placards be used?

options.text: Any time a vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
If there is open space in the truck.
If the amount of hazardous materials in the truck exceeds 200 pounds.
If the hazardous materials create an inhalation hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show what type of material is being carried and warn others of any dangers.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum permitted total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
The minimum permitted weight of a trailer
The maximum permitted weight of a trailer and its contents
The maximum permitted weight of only a tractor

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum permitted total weight of a vehicle and its cargo
questions.explanation: The GVWR is the heaviest your vehicle and its load can weigh. This maximum weight is set by the manufacturer.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: By tapping on the brake pedal three times
By pushing in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: By pushing in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: Modern air brake vehicles have a yellow diamond-shaped knob for the parking brake. Pull it out to set the brake. Push it in to release the brake.

questions.question: What is the maximum leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: Know the maximum air loss rate that is safe for your vehicle. For a triple combination vehicle, the leakage rate should not exceed 6 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allow you to drive faster than you would be able to otherwise.
Allow you to follow other vehicles more closely than you would be able to otherwise.
Allow you to drive less carefully than you would be able to otherwise.

questions.explanation: ABS helps you keep control during hard braking. It does not necessarily make your vehicle stop faster.

questions.question: What might a vehicle stopped at a green light indicate about the driver?

options.text: Does not know the rules of the road.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who are drunk, tired, on drugs, or sick can be dangerous. Stopping at a green light is one sign that a driver may be impaired.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder for safety?

options.text: When you are carrying a passenger
When you are carrying a heavy load

questions.explanation: A retarder is a device that helps slow your vehicle without using the brakes. However, a retarder can cause your wheels to skid on slippery surfaces. Turn it off when driving on wet, snowy, or icy roads.

questions.question: What is reaction distance?

options.text: The distance traveled between seeing a hazard and physically hitting the brakes
The distance traveled between a hazard becoming visible and a driver seeing the hazard
The distance traveled before a driver realizes they must brake
The distance traveled between physically hitting the brake and coming to a complete stop

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance traveled between seeing a hazard and physically hitting the brakes
questions.explanation: Reaction distance is how far your vehicle travels from when you see a hazard until you actually press the brake pedal.

questions.question: When may brakes get out of adjustment?
questions.explanation: Brakes can get out of adjustment quickly if they become too hot from heavy use. Check your brake adjustment regularly.

questions.question: When driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hide your intentions from other drivers.
Use turn signals only when other vehicles are near.
Do not use turn signals in construction zones.
Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: You must tell other drivers what you plan to do. Signal before turning or changing lanes, even if no other cars are nearby.

questions.question: Why must you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air becomes old and needs to be replaced.
Because compressed air contains water that must be removed from the tanks.
To remove bad air from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be removed from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and compressor oil. If left in the system, water and oil can damage the brakes. You must drain tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the maximum air leakage during a static leakage test is ____ per minute.
questions.explanation: For a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate must not exceed 5 psi per minute during a static leakage test. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repair and should not be driven.

questions.question: Which item is required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes: at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles such as reflective triangles.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how does this affect braking distance?
questions.explanation: Higher speed increases how far your vehicle travels before stopping. When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, your braking distance becomes four times longer.

questions.question: How should you test a parking brake?

options.text: The engine should not be running.
Put the vehicle in a low gear and try to pull forward while the parking brake is set.
Have a professional mechanic inspect it.
Drive the vehicle with the parking brake applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in a low gear and try to pull forward while the parking brake is set.
questions.explanation: To test a parking brake: fasten your safety belt, set the parking brake, release the trailer parking brake if needed, put the vehicle in low gear, and try to pull forward. If the parking brake does not hold, it must be repaired.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through fog?
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: How can you best reduce cell phone distractions while driving?

options.text: Stay on one call for the entire trip.
Turn the phone off before driving.
Only use the phone to accept incoming calls.
Use text messages instead of calls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the phone off before driving.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid cell phone distractions is to turn off your phone before you start driving and keep it off until you reach your destination.

questions.question: For a single vehicle with air brakes, what is the maximum air leakage during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate must not exceed 3 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: When entering traffic on an expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Abruptly enter a lane of traffic.
Cut off other drivers if necessary.

questions.explanation: When entering an expressway during the skills test, you must check for traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the correct lane.

questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: You cannot see clearly behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.
Extra weight may be in the front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see clearly behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. If you must back up, ask someone to help guide you if possible.

questions.question: During an engine fire, which action should you NOT take?
questions.explanation: During an engine fire, turn off the engine right away. Do not open the hood if you can avoid it. Spray foam through the louvers or from under the vehicle instead.

questions.question: What should you do when backing?

options.text: Move quickly to stay out of other drivers' way.

questions.explanation: Backing a large truck is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Ask someone to help guide you if you must back up.

questions.question: If you drive a truck that requires a CDL::

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only when driving a tank trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: For your safety, you must wear your seat belt at all times while operating a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: During the steering box inspection, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that the steering box is securely mounted.
Check that the steering box has no leaks.
Look for missing bolts in the steering box.
Assume all cotter keys are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that the steering box is securely mounted. Look for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Make sure there are no power steering fluid leaks and no damage to the hoses.

questions.question: When driving down a hill, when should you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: As you pick up speed going downhill.
Near the bottom of the hill.

questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before driving downhill. Shifting into a lower gear at high speed can damage your transmission and prevent engine braking. Drive at a safe speed that lets you control your vehicle without overusing the brakes. Consider the hill's steepness, length, your vehicle's weight, road conditions, and weather.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: Hold air for only one braking cycle.
Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops.
Hold enough air for more than 1,000 braking cycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the air storage tanks hold enough air for the brakes to work several times even if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: When driving with cargo, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and check the cargo within the first 50 miles.
Ask other drivers about their loads.
Use only the side mirrors to check the cargo.
Skip checking the cargo if it was secured before starting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check the cargo within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Inspect the cargo and securing devices before starting your trip. After starting, check the cargo and securing devices within the first 50 miles, every 3 hours or 150 miles of travel, and after every break.

questions.question: If your vehicle has power steering, what should you check on the hoses?

options.text: That they are connected to the battery.
That they have the proper amount of play.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a vehicle with power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Specifically look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: Where is the tire load rating located?

options.text: On the inside of the driver's door.
On the side of each tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of each tire.
questions.explanation: The tire load rating is the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a specific pressure. This number is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains that remove water and compressor oil. These substances can damage the brakes if they build up in the system.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube used to move air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes when used
A part within the braking unit that allows air to move freely

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi.

questions.question: While driving:

options.text: A driver does not need to inform others of their intentions.
A driver should only use turn signals if a vehicle is next to them.
A driver should not use a turn signal if their lane change will be obvious.
A driver should always use turn signals to inform others of their intentions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver should always use turn signals to inform others of their intentions.
questions.explanation: Always use turn signals. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing:

options.text: You will likely be able to outdrive a train.
You should not rely only on warning signals.
You should roll a window down to listen for an approaching train.
You should only worry about the track closest to your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should not rely only on warning signals.
questions.explanation: Do not rely only on warning signals to tell you a train is coming. Never try to race a train. If there are multiple tracks, check all tracks in both directions before crossing.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, weight should be:

options.text: Placed only on the left side, if possible.
Placed only on the right side, if possible.

questions.explanation: Load cargo as low as possible in the trailer. Placing weight too high increases the risk of the vehicle tipping over.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a sign of a person being drowsy?
questions.explanation: Signs of drowsiness include frequent blinking, eyes closing or losing focus, yawning, and drifting between lanes. Avoid driving drowsy.

questions.question: After the engine is started, warning lights and buzzers should all:

options.text: Turn off once the vehicle begins moving.

questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off immediately when the engine starts. This includes the charging circuit warning light, oil light, coolant light, and ABS light.

questions.question: Why should the steps of a pre-trip inspection be done in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget a step.
The form must be followed in order.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget a step.
questions.explanation: Following the same steps each time helps you learn and remember the inspection. A routine makes it less likely you will skip a step.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back parking, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: Hydroplaning usually occurs:

options.text: In areas where water collects on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: In areas where water collects on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water builds up on the road. Low tire pressure and worn tire tread increase the risk. It can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph.
